text:
elaine-support: Heads up — AcmeCorp opened an escalation: after a corp firewall rules push they see repeated mTLS handshake failures to our private control plane (vpc.cp.redwood). Errors: repeated TLS alert 40 / handshake_failure and connection reset. Customer says it started after their NGFW update.

matt-eng: Can you paste the openssl s_client output and any tcpdump? Curious if SNI/ALPN or client cert are getting stripped.

elaine-support: Pasting the s_client output they provided (redacted IPs):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.1.2.3:443 -tls1_3 -servername vpc.cp.redwood
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = controlplane.redwood.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
    Session-ID: 
    Session-ID-ctx: 
    Master-Key: XXXXX
    Start Time: 1670000000
    Timeout   : 7200 (sec)
    Verify return code: 20 (unable to get local issuer certificate)
```
But tcpdump shows ClientHello then server sends TLS alert 40 shortly after. Also customer tcpdump: `TLSv1.3  ? Handshake Protocol: Client Hello, length 256` then `Alert (Level: Fatal, Description: handshake_failure)`.

sanjay-privatenet: Two quick possibilities: 1) NGFW is performing TLS inspection and rewriting/removing extensions (ALPN, SNI, supported_groups or key_share) — that will break TLS1.3 handshakes. 2) A proxy is truncating the client cert chain or dropping client certificate negotiation. Which side is terminating TLS? If their egress proxy terminates and re-initiates TLS, it must present a valid client cert or allow passthrough.

matt-eng: Also check for ClientHello fragmentation — some edge proxies reassemble poorly and drop extensions. Ask them to run `tcpdump -s 0 -w dump.pcap host 10.1.2.3 and port 443` and share a pcap. If the ClientHello is fragmented or missing ALPN (`h2,http/1.1`) we will see it.

elaine-support: Customer attached a pcap. Quick grep shows ALPN absent in the post-firewall trace. Pre-firewall host-to-proxy shows ALPN present. So the NGFW appears to strip ALPN. They also have a TLS-inspect appliance that swaps certs.

deploy-bot: [control-plane] Incoming connection from 10.1.2.3 failed mTLS verification: "client_certificate_required" — auth rejected.

karen-customer-success: I pinged the customer; they confirm they must enable corporate TLS inspection for auditing. They can create an exception for specific IPs. Are there IPs/ports we can give them to narrow the allowlist?

matt-eng: Provide them our control plane FQDNs and the static egress IP ranges used by their dedicated region, and ask them to allow passthrough (no TLS inspect) to those IPs on 443. Also if they cannot disable inspection, they must install a subordinate CA on our side — which we don't accept. So passthrough/allowlist is the only supported option.

sanjay-privatenet: Actionable repro steps for customer: (1) From a host behind the NGFW, run `openssl s_client -connect vpc.cp.redwood:443 -tls1_3 -servername vpc.cp.redwood -alpn h2` and capture. (2) From the same host but bypassing the NGFW/proxy (if possible), run the same. Compare ClientHello ALPN and supported_groups/key_share. If NGFW removed ALPN or key_share groups -> TLS1.3 handshake will fail with handshake_failure.

elaine-support: Customer attempted to add an allowlist for our IPs but still saw failures — they later confirmed the NGFW clamps TLS and performs MITM even for allowlisted ranges unless passthrough is explicitly enabled. They will try explicit passthrough.

matt-eng: Also ask them to ensure OCSP/CRL fetching is allowed (outbound TCP to 80/443) and that intermediate certs are not dropped. In our logs we sometimes see `no peer certificate` when the proxy strips the chain.

incidents-bot: Incident #INC-2026-483 created: "Cust mTLS fails due to NGFW TLS inspection (AcmeCorp)" — assigned to eng-infra, priority P2.

elaine-support: Next steps agreed with customer: 1) customer will configure TLS passthrough for our control plane IPs and test. 2) if still failing, they'll provide full pcap and NAT trace (ingress/egress) plus proxy config. 3) we'll collect server-side logs and open a private escalation with eng-infra.

matt-eng: If they can't do passthrough, workaround is to run Redwood Private in a dedicated connectivity model where control plane is reachable via VPN/Direct Connect — not ideal but an option.

karen-customer-success: I'll coordinate the test window with AcmeCorp for tomorrow 10:00PT and stay on the call for hand-holding.

elaine-support: Closing loop here for now — if customer confirms passthrough fixes it we'll mark resolved; otherwise we escalate to eng-infra with pcaps and our server logs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
